subject: Post-demo follow-up: concurrency & streaming targets + Redwood rate/quota proposal
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Patrick O'Leary <patrick@currents.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: concurrency & streaming targets + Redwood rate/quota proposal

Hi Patrick — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can lock POC sizing and a short-term quota bump for testing.

Recap (what I heard):
- Primary workload: streaming real-time transcript enrichment (chunked responses) into 3 consumer endpoints (ingest, enrichment, archiver).
- Target latency: P95 end-to-end generation latency ~<300ms for 512-token windows (interactive feel).
- Steady throughput target: ~200 req/s during business hours, with sustained bursts up to ~450 req/s during peak; concurrency of ~120 simultaneous streaming connections expected, with occasional spikes to 400 during batch imports.
- Global footprint: primary region us-east, DR in eu-west.

Open items for us to confirm:
1) Are the "simultaneous streaming connections" independent long-lived connections (keep-alive + chunked streaming), or short-lived poll-and-close?
2) Average tokens per request and typical response chunk cadence (you said ~6 chunks/request on average — can you confirm)?
3) Any hard SLA requirements for tail latency (e.g., 99th percentile target) beyond the P95 above?

Attached: Currents-POC-MAP-v1.pdf (mutual action plan) and currents-mrp-matrix.xlsx (rough concurrency/traffic matrix).

Proposed short-term path from Redwood:
- Temporary quota bump on hosted keys to support POC: double default QPS & connections for 2 weeks while we run load tests.
- Suggested technical approach for POC: keep-alive connection pooling + per-connection streaming (continuous chunking).
- If production sizing holds, recommend Dedicated reserved pool (or a hybrid: dedicated frontends + hosted fallback) — we can rough-scope GPU count once we have confirmed average token rates.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm items #1-#3 above by end of day tomorrow?
- If yes, Ben & Marissa and I will run a brief cost/scale estimate and propose a temporary quota plan + a Dedicated sizing sketch.

Thanks — Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

From: Patrick O'Leary <patrick@currents.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@currents.ai>
Date: 2027-11-05T10:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: concurrency & streaming targets + Redwood rate/quota proposal

Thanks Vivek — good summary. Quick clarifications:

- Streaming model: yes, long-lived HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections with chunked transfer encoding. Clients keep a single connection per worker process; average 1.2 worker processes per host, roughly 120 hosts at peak.
- Chunks: on average 5–7 chunks per request, majority of responses ~400 tokens total.
- Tail: 99th percentile is important for the UI — we want 99th < 750ms if possible; P95 < 300ms remains the main KPI though.
- Regions: primary us-east, but traffic distribution is ~85% us-east, 15% eu-west.

Procurement: can you share examples of how Redwood typically structures a temporary quota/ad-hoc bump for POCs (duration, rollback)?

Happy to do a tech sync — next 2 days open except for tomorrow morning.

— Patrick
Patrick O'Leary
Head of Platform Engineering | Currents AI
patrick@currents.ai | +1 (617) 555-1324

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Patrick O'Leary <patrick@currents.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-05T13:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: concurrency & streaming targets + Redwood rate/quota proposal

Appreciate the details — helpful. Answering both technical + procurement parts below.

Technical:
- Long-lived keep-alive streaming is ideal — Redwood supports chunked streaming over persistent connections and we have optimizations for continuous KV-cached sessions that reduce generation overhead for multi-chunk requests.
- Based on 400 tokens avg and 5–7 chunks, rough POC sizing for hosted (conservative): default shared endpoints may hit rate-limits once you exceed ~100 concurrent streaming connections per API key. For your POC we recommend either: (A) temporary per-key quota bump (to ~500 concurrent streams + corresponding QPS) OR (B) Dedicated reserved pool (recommended for production) sized for ~250 concurrent streams steady-state with autoscale burst to 500.
- Tail latency: we can target P99 < 750ms with Dedicated pool + autoscaling and preferential kernel selection; hosted may meet P95 < 300ms but P99 can be variable under noisy neighbors unless you purchase Dedicated capacity.
- Connection pooling guidance: use a small pool per host (2–4 connections) and multiplex many logical sessions per connection only for non-streaming flows — since you need true chunked streaming we expect 1 connection per active stream. We'll provide suggested connection pool config (attached: proposed-connpool-config.yaml).

Procurement / quota bump process:
- POC bump: 14-day temporary quota increase, refundable if excessive usage observed; typically requires a short intake form and a mutual action plan. We can issue the bump the same day we sign the MAP.
- Pricing: for short POCs we often do a consumption-forward pricing estimate plus a capped overage rate; Ben will draft three options (small/medium/large POC buckets).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I will send a tech-deep call invite for tomorrow afternoon with our infra engineer if that works.
2) Ben/Marissa to share a pricing sketch and a specific temporary quota ask (numbers we propose: 500 concurrent streams, QPS 1,000, tokens/sec budget of 10k) — please confirm if those look reasonable.
3) We will attach a short runbook for test traffic and a Doc: example load script + expected monitoring points (latency P95/P99, error rates, connection rejected counts).

Ben / Marissa: please prepare the POC pricing sketch and MAP sign-off form.

Vivek

[Attachments: proposed-connpool-config.yaml]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: concurrency & streaming targets + Redwood rate/quota proposal

Patrick — I'll run numbers and have three POC buckets by EOD tomorrow:
- Option A: POC Lite — 200 concurrent streams, QPS 400, tokens/sec 4k (low cost)
- Option B: POC Standard — 500 concurrent streams, QPS 1k, tokens/sec 10k (recommended)
- Option C: POC Aggressive — 1k concurrent streams, burst to 2k QPS (for heavy import windows)

I'll include estimated costs and a short clause for a 14-day temporary bump and rollback. Vivek: please add the MAP link and the suggested test window.

Ben Carter
